channel_dna.platform_type: Real-time community platform with servers, channels, voice, and text. Originally gaming, now dominant for developer communities, crypto, creator communities, and product user bases.
channel_dna.algorithm_type: No public algorithm. Discovery through Server Discovery feature (minimum 200 members), community invites, website/product integration, and word-of-mouth. Members must be actively invited.
channel_dna.primary_audience: Developer communities (very strong), gaming and creator communities, Web3/crypto, study communities, product user communities. Ages 16-35 skew. Highly engaged active users.
channel_dna.native_content_formats: Text channels (like Slack), voice channels, video, threads, forums (new feature), bots and automation, stage channels for announcements. Rich link embeds. Bots are a major community tool.
channel_dna.platform_culture_code: Real-time, informal, community-focused. Server culture varies wildly. Member roles and hierarchy create status. Bots automate moderation and add fun. Active servers have thriving sub-communities in different channels. Dead servers are ghost towns.
channel_dna.account_warmup_requirements: Build a proper server structure before inviting anyone. Set up roles, channels, rules, and welcome message. Add basic bots (MEE6 or Carl-bot for moderation). Have at least 5-10 real members having genuine conversations before promoting broadly.

fit_scoring_matrix.best_product_types: Developer tools, gaming adjacent, AI/ML communities, Web3 products, study and edtech tools, creator tools, products where community is a core value proposition
fit_scoring_matrix.worst_product_types: B2B enterprise software where buyers are not community-oriented, local services, consumer products for 40+ demographic with low Discord adoption
fit_scoring_matrix.best_pricing_models: Discord community works with all pricing models — it is a retention and community channel, not primarily a conversion channel. Free tier users convert better to paid through community.
fit_scoring_matrix.icp_match_signals: Search '[product category] Discord server' — if servers with 1K+ members exist for your category, your ICP is using Discord. Join these servers before building your own.
fit_scoring_matrix.red_flags_skip_this_channel: Skip if you cannot commit to active moderation and community management. A dead Discord is worse than no Discord. Skip if your ICP is not Discord-native.
fit_scoring_matrix.geographic_strength: US, UK, Brazil, France, Germany dominant. Global gaming and developer communities. Strong in Southeast Asia.

growth_mechanics.expected_cac: $0 cash for community members. Discord servers are retention and community channels — CAC happens through other channels, Discord reduces churn.
growth_mechanics.time_to_first_traffic_spike: N/A — Discord is not a traffic generation channel. It is a community and retention channel.
growth_mechanics.time_to_first_paying_user: Discord community members convert to paid at significantly higher rates (2-5x) than non-community users. But conversion comes through the product, not Discord itself.
growth_mechanics.effort_level: Very High. Active community management daily. Moderation. Content in channels. Events (AMAs, voice chats). Discord communities fail without daily attention.
growth_mechanics.virality_coefficient: Low for new member acquisition. High for retention — active community members become product evangelists who bring others.
growth_mechanics.compounding_potential: High — a thriving Discord community is an enormous competitive moat. Users in active communities churn 60-80% less than non-community users.

algorithm_playbook.how_reach_is_determined: Server Discovery ranking based on member count and activity. Invite links shared in other platforms (Reddit, Twitter, Dev.to). In-product invite prompts. Server Boosts increase visibility.
algorithm_playbook.what_algorithm_rewards: Active servers with daily message volume. Servers with high member retention (people not leaving). Server Boosts (paid feature that increases Discovery ranking).
algorithm_playbook.what_kills_reach: Dead channels with no activity. Servers where the only person talking is a bot. Over-moderation that kills organic conversation. Too many rules that intimidate new members.
algorithm_playbook.peak_posting_windows: No algorithm to optimise. Focus on community events at times when your members are most active. Check Discord server analytics for your server's peak hours.
algorithm_playbook.optimal_posting_cadence: Daily announcements or discussions in key channels. Weekly community events (AMA, voice chat, demo). Real-time response to member questions (within 2-4 hours during business hours).
algorithm_playbook.content_freshness_window: Real-time — Discord is live conversation. Old messages scroll away. Pin important messages. Use threads for focused discussions.

content_system.winning_content_types: 1. #announcements channel (product updates, launches) 2. #showcase (user creations with your product) 3. #feedback (structured feedback collection) 4. #general (organic community conversation) 5. #help (support and Q&A) 6. Weekly community events (AMAs, demos, voice chats)
content_system.hook_formulas: Server invite: 'Join 2,000 [product] users who [specific value prop].' Welcome message: 'Welcome! Start here: [#start-here channel link]. Ask anything in [#general].' Announcement format: 'What is new: [specific feature]. Why it matters: [benefit]. Try it: [link].'
content_system.platform_native_tone: Casual, real-time, community-first. Informal. Emojis are native here. Voice chats add a human element. Founders participating in #general as community members (not just broadcasting) is the most effective approach.
content_system.cta_approach: Discord is a retention tool, not a conversion tool. CTA = get them to invite a friend or try a new feature. In #announcements: link to changelog or new feature. Upgrade CTAs should be rare and contextual.
content_system.content_to_avoid: Only using Discord to broadcast announcements. Not responding to member messages. Auto-welcome messages with no human follow-up. Over-moderation that deletes genuine questions.
content_system.cross_posting_rules: Product updates posted on Twitter/LinkedIn should also be posted in Discord #announcements. Discord conversations (interesting feature requests, testimonials) can be shared on Twitter with member permission.

community_outreach_playbook.where_icp_clusters: Join 10 Discord servers in your product category BEFORE building your own. Understand what good communities look like. Observe what your ICP discusses.
community_outreach_playbook.contribution_before_pitch_rule: Be helpful in other relevant Discord servers for weeks before promoting your own. Drop genuine value, answer questions, share resources. Never spam your server invite in others' servers.
community_outreach_playbook.dm_outreach_approach: Discord DMs for direct user outreach — after someone asks a question your product solves in a community server, DM with a helpful answer and soft mention of your product. High conversion when genuinely helpful.
community_outreach_playbook.influencer_partner_strategy: Partner with popular Discord servers in your category — offer exclusive perks for their members (discount code, special role). Server owners are the influencers here.
community_outreach_playbook.broadcast_vs_community_mode: Community mode entirely. Discord is the anti-broadcast channel. Every feature should serve the community, not the company.
community_outreach_playbook.banned_behaviours: Raiding other servers. Self-promotion without permission in others' servers. Buying fake Discord members. NSFW content in non-NSFW servers. IP violations.

business_stage_playbook.pre_launch_0_users: Do NOT build a Discord server until you have a product. Premature Discord servers die instantly. Use it for closed beta community if you have 20+ beta users already.
business_stage_playbook.early_traction_1_to_100: Launch Discord server with first 50-100 users. Invite personally. Be extremely active. This small group becomes the cultural foundation of your entire community.
business_stage_playbook.growth_100_to_1k: Structure channels properly. Add moderation bots. Create roles for power users. Host first community events. Apply for Discord Server Discovery once you hit 200 members.
business_stage_playbook.scale_1k_plus: Hire a community manager. Partner with related servers for cross-promotion. Apply for Discord Partner or Verified Server status. Create tiered roles (free vs paid users get different channels).

proof_of_play.early_stage_win: Midjourney — built their entire early user base through a Discord server. Every user interaction happened in Discord. The community-first approach created massive word-of-mouth growth that cost $0 in paid acquisition.
proof_of_play.growth_stage_win: Supabase Discord — 35K+ members. Developer community answers questions faster than official support. Community-led support reduces churn dramatically and the word-of-mouth from happy community members drives significant new user acquisition.
proof_of_play.what_made_it_work: Both treated the community as the product, not a marketing channel. The Discord was the first place members went — not the last resort.
proof_of_play.what_would_have_killed_it: A Discord server used only for broadcast announcements with no genuine community interaction would have been abandoned within 30 days.
